source: NCERT Class XI, Indian Economic Development, Ch. 6 (Employment: Growth, Informalisation and Other Issues).

sections.heading: 1. Workers and the Workforce
points: A **worker** = a person engaged in an economic activity for pay or profit (or helping in a family enterprise).
**Workforce participation rate** = proportion of the population that is working.
**Self-employed, casual wage labourers, and regular salaried** are the three main categories; most Indian workers are **self-employed or casual**.

sections.heading: 2. Structure of Employment
points: Employment is spread across **primary (agriculture — still the largest employer), secondary and tertiary** sectors.
There is a **structural shift** — the share of agriculture in employment is slowly falling, and services/industry rising, but agriculture still employs the most.
**Rural vs urban** and **men vs women** participation differ; women's participation is under-counted.

sections.heading: 3. Formal and Informal Sectors — Informalisation
points: **Formal (organised) sector** — registered enterprises (public + private employing 10+); **job security, benefits, regulation**.
**Informal (unorganised) sector** — small units, no security or benefits; **the vast majority** of Indian workers are here.
**Informalisation/casualisation** — the growing share of informal, insecure, casual jobs (even in the formal sector, contract labour rises).
Informal workers need **social security and protection**.

sections.heading: 4. Unemployment and Government Measures
points: Measured by the **NSSO** (usual status, weekly status, daily status).
**Jobless growth** — output grows but jobs don't.
Government schemes: **MGNREGA (100 days rural work)**, skill development, self-employment programmes.

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Worker categories: self-employed, casual wage, regular salaried; most Indians self-employed/casual.
Agriculture = still the largest employer (share slowly falling).
Formal (organised) = secure/registered; Informal (unorganised) = majority, insecure.
Informalisation/casualisation = rising insecure jobs.
Types of unemployment: disguised, seasonal, open, educated; MGNREGA = 100 days.

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: The **majority of Indian workers are in the informal (unorganised) sector**.
**Agriculture is still the largest employer** (though its share is declining).
**Disguised unemployment** = surplus labour (common in agriculture).
**Jobless growth** = output rises without matching job creation.
